Genetics confirmed a homozygous pathogenic ENPP1 variant and a heterozygous pathogenic ALPL variant consistent with hypophosphatasia; he had tooth loss, aortic and pulmonary arterial calcification and bilateral medullary nephrocalcinosis.
Oral calcitriol and phosphate were followed by clinical improvement and normalization of phosphate levels.

summary.text: A clinical diagnosis of GACI was made antenatally after calcifications on ultrasound at 29 wk gestation, with an older affected sibling who died at 4 days of life; maternal etidronate was commenced from 29 wk gestation.

Extensive arterial calcifications were present at birth; bisphosphonates were given after birth until 8 mo of age, calcifications gradually improved and she subsequently developed rickets, treated with phosphate and calcitriol from 2 yr of age.

Later problems included nephrocalcinosis, internal carotid narrowing requiring aspirin from five years of age, generalized dental hypoplasia with crown placement, and at 7 yr focal status epilepticus, aphasia and right sided hemiparesis with left parietal ischemia, followed by neurological improvement after revascularization.

summary.text: A 3-month-old male presented to the general practitioner with poor feeding and abnormal movements, deteriorated in the Emergency Department needing cardiac compressions and developed cardiogenic shock with absent pulses in NICU.

CT showed widespread calcifications of large and medium-sized arteries and a homozygous ENPP1 pathogenic variant was confirmed; bisphosphonate treatment was commenced prior to genetic confirmation, he continues on etidronate, and compassionate access to ENPP1 enzyme replacement is in progress.

summary.text: A 2-wk-old infant presented with right shoulder discomfort noted since birth; X-ray, MRI and CT showed glenohumeral joint calcification and extensive multifocal vascular calcification, with no coronary calcification on echocardiogram or CT cardiac angiogram and dysplastic kidneys on renal ultrasound.

A homozygous ENPP1 pathogenic variant was confirmed; the vascular calcifications improved without treatment over the first year of life, rickets was noted at 15 mo, and calcitriol and oral phosphate were commenced at 2 yr of age; enrolment in an ENPP1 enzyme replacement trial is planned.
